newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resids steady to down again, trade thin.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resids steady to down again, trade thin.

text.p: U.S. spot fuel oil prices were unchanged to lower again Monday despite steady crude, with mild East Coast weather and prospects for better high sulphur avails pressuring some grades, industry sources said.

"I think we're in retreat. There's very little demand and there's some high sulphur coming to the East Coast," said one cash trader, noting 6-10 day forecasts were calling for mostly seasonal East Coast weather.
At the U.S. Gulf, prices again lost ground, with one percent down another 40 cents to about $19 a barrel. USG three percent was down a quarter to about $18.25, traders said.
A Florida utility tendered for up to 180,000 barrels of one percent, 1.8 percent and/or 2.2 percent material for delivery prior to Dec 20. Bids are due Tuesday at 1400 EST.
In New York Harbor, high sulphurs were pressured by still-soft bunkers, with 2.2 percent down 25 cents to $20.00-25 and three percent off slightly to $19.25-50.
NYH physical one percent again was unchanged at about $21.25, with November and December paper quotes steady with crude at about $21 and low-$21, respectively.
No NYH or USG deals were confirmed.

Forecasts for colder Midwest weather later this week and next helped firm November New York City gate gas prices Monday by about 20 cents to $3.40/mmBtu versus NYH November one percent resid paper at a $3.33/mmBtu equivalent.
